# Fusion scenario-editor UI redesign — project notes

> This file is a synced copy of a Claude Code memory file (`fusion-scenario-editor-redesign.md`) kept so GitHub Copilot has the same context. Claude's copy is the source of truth — whenever it's updated, this file should be updated to match in the same edit/commit. If the two ever disagree, trust the Claude memory file and re-sync this one.
>
> This is a scoped Copilot instructions file (`.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`), not the repo-wide `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, so it only gets applied when Copilot is working on files under `help/workfront-fusion/`, not on every request in the repo.

## Confirmed new-experience UI facts (no screenshot needed to reuse these)

- Hover over the right edge of a module → an **Add another module** button appears → click it → opens the app/service picker (same picker as adding the first module).
- Right-click a module → Settings context menu (order): Run this module only / **Add error handler** / Rename / Clone / Copy module / Add a note / Copy mapping / Copy module name / App metadata / **Delete module**. Both confirmed unchanged from classic.
- Left-click the path between two modules → the **Set up a filter** window opens directly. Right-clicking the same path opens a different (fuller) context menu instead — not a menu with "Set up a filter" as an option.
- Right-click a path → **Add a router** and **Add a module** are both options (see `add-a-module-between-modules.png`).
- **Copy filter** / **Paste filter** (via right-click a path that already has a filter) still exist and work the same way — visually restyled to match the new card canvas, but same options/labels.
- Clicking the Router module itself (not hovering its edge) still adds a new route — confirmed unchanged.
- **Order routes** (right-click the Router module → "Order routes" → drag and drop) — confirmed still valid, unchanged from classic.
- **Disable route** (right-click a route's path → "Disable route") and the disabled-route visual (gray path + disabled-route icon on the label) — confirmed unchanged from classic.
- The Router module ("Flow Control" > "Router") is filed under the **Built-in** category in the new picker (also appears under "All apps," but Built-in is the category to cite in instructions).
- Fallback route: unlike classic (which marks it with a distinct arrow on the Router module itself), the new experience marks the fallback route by displaying **"Fallback"** in green text on the route's label — no arrow-marker screenshot needed for this fact.
- Error handler route: unlike classic (transparent vs. solid circles), the new experience marks an error handler route with a dotted line and a red **"Error handler"** label — no screenshot needed for this fact.
- Module name corrections (actual Workfront names, not typos carried from older drafts): **"Watch Record"** (singular, not "Watch Records"), **"Update a record"** (not "Update Record").
- Still unconfirmed and blocking `debug-a-scenario.md` + a few other articles: whether the **DevTool** is being removed from the new experience at all (heard as a rumor, no other detail yet — see the Feature comparison sheet, "DevTool" row).

## House conventions established for this redesign (apply to every remaining article)

- Full parallel duplication: one H2/H3 tree for "...in the new experience (Recommended)" and a separate one for "...in the classic experience," with `(Classic)` suffixes anywhere needed to avoid anchor collisions. Add a mini-TOC under any heading that now has 2+ children.
- Collapse the "new vs. classic" explanation into a single `>[!NOTE]` at the **end of the article's intro** (not its own H2), reusing this exact wording, with "in the article Scenario editor" appended to the link:
  > Workfront Fusion is transitioning the scenario editor to a new experience. During this transition, both the classic and new experiences are available, and you can switch between them at any time. We recommend using the new experience. For more information, see [New and classic experiences](/help/workfront-fusion/get-started-with-fusion/navigate-fusion/scenario-editor.md#new-and-classic-experiences) in the article Scenario editor.
- The new-experience heading carries `(Recommended)` (e.g. `## Add a filter in the new experience (Recommended)`).
- Content that's genuinely UI-agnostic (e.g. the `?moduleId=` URL-parameter note in `add-a-module-basic.md`) doesn't need duplicating — use judgment, but check with Becky first if unsure (she's pushed back before when a note was moved without asking).
- If Becky confirms a whole procedure is identical between experiences (not just a UI-agnostic note), don't split it into new/classic H2/H3s at all — collapse to a single procedure using the new-experience wording (e.g. `view-scenario-data-flow.md`'s "View data flow in a running scenario"). Default assumption is still that procedures differ and need splitting — only collapse after explicit confirmation.
- For a single illustrative screenshot (not a full step-by-step procedure) where the new and classic visuals genuinely differ, don't pick one or flag-and-wait — show both, new first: a plain-text label line ("New experience" / "Classic experience") immediately above each image, new experience first. Mention the new-experience behavior first in the surrounding prose too (e.g. "...marked by X in the new experience, or by Y in the classic experience"), not just in the image labels. See `view-scenario-data-flow.md`'s running/output indicators.
- Flag anything unconfirmed inline as `<!-- BECKY CHECK ME: ... -->` right at the spot — never a visible callout.
- Once every flag in an article is resolved, mark that row `Yes` in the tracking spreadsheet's "Affected articles" sheet (column G). Use `In progress` if only some flags are resolved.
